column2: If the audience laughs, that is art!
If you will look after my whole company, I am in.
Head of a travelling troupe; actor, singer and librettist. From 1789 he ran the Theater auf der Wieden in Vienna, and in 1791 he wrote the libretto of Die Zauberflöte and played Papageno himself.
A sailor's song? I shall have them weeping in the harbour taverns.
Singing and playing alone, I shall draw you a crowd.
Composer, singer and actor. From 1789 he won popularity with 'table entertainments', in which he sang and accompanied himself alone. His songs about sailors are said to have helped naval recruiting.
Music that does not keep the rules of counterpoint is not music.
Allow me to teach your players counterpoint.
Organist at the Viennese court, later Kapellmeister of St Stephen's Cathedral. He taught the young Beethoven counterpoint, and wrote strict textbooks of theory.
Once the customers in the tavern start dancing, we have won.
Wherever you let me play waltzes.

A master of the waltz who started out with a small band playing in Viennese taverns. The young Johann Strauss (the elder) was one of his players, but set up on his own in 1825 and became his greatest rival.
In the last galop — let the pistols fire!
Leave the ball to me and Paris will be in ferment.

A conductor of dance music who drew crowds at the masked balls of the Paris Opéra. For flamboyant effects such as pistol shots and smashed chairs at the end of a piece, he was called 'Napoléon Musard'. From 1833 he also gave cheap promenade concerts.
My songs are liked by the people rather than by kings.
Poking fun at the world in song is what I do best.
A writer of chansons beloved of the people. He was imprisoned twice for satirising the monarchy in song, and each time his popularity grew.
The director of the Conservatoire — play in the street?
For a disciplined orchestra, I shall lend a hand.

Director of the Paris Conservatoire (1822–42). Stern and feared, in 1823 he refused the 12-year-old Liszt admission 'because he is a foreigner'. Beethoven revered him as the foremost composer of the day.
March down the street and everyone follows.
Let me play you a sound schooled in the military band.
A Viennese military bandmaster and composer of waltzes and marches. A rival of the Strauss family, he later became the last music director of the Viennese court balls.
The Opéra? My public is waiting in the cafés.
I shall take the songs of the street onto a big stage.
Real name Emma Valladon. In the 1860s she was the sensation of the Paris café-concert Alcazar. Invited to fashionable salons too, she was called 'the queen of the café-concert'.
A tune you can whistle is the best tune of all.
In the theatre or in church, I can be of use.

In 1875 the comic opera Trial by Jury, written with the librettist Gilbert, was a great hit. The songs from their works were so popular that they were whistled on the street corners of London. His song 'The Lost Chord' was a huge success too.
I cannot read music, but I know a song the customers will like.
If you let me sing somewhere bigger than a saloon.

An immigrant boy born in Russia. In his teens he was a singing waiter in a saloon in New York's Chinatown. He could play the piano only on the black keys (F-sharp major) and later used a special piano with a shifting keyboard.
I have known what an audience feels since I sang down the pit.
I shall bring you the whole music-hall public.
A singer who rose from Scottish coal miner to great star of the music hall. His Scottish songs, sung in a kilt, were hugely popular.
The music hall is hotter than the opera house.
When I appear, I fill the house.
Queen of the Paris music hall. She starred in the revues of the Casino de Paris and the Moulin Rouge. Legend has it that she insured her celebrated legs.
With tunes people can hum, I want to make the world dance.
An operetta orchestra? Leave it to me.
Originally a military bandmaster. His operetta Die lustige Witwe (The Merry Widow), first performed at the Theater an der Wien in Vienna in December 1905, became a worldwide hit.
